achievements.text: Shipped Professional Mode for Facebook Creators as EM of a team of 10. Owned composer, settings, and onboarding surfaces. Onboarded ΞM creators in the first 3 months, unlocking α% of the org's top-line annual goal at β× target.

Led 10 ICs on the Bulletin Publishing UI team through its scale-up and ultimate sunset. Placed every UI engineer who needed a new team, then rebuilt mine around the back-end work that became Professional Mode.

items.caption: Facebook Professional Mode (2023). Opt-in creator surface that bundled monetization, analytics, audience tools, and safety controls into one home for people building on Facebook. Letting anyone on Facebook become a creator on the platform.

Bulletin (2021). Meta's independent newsletter platform for paid writers: discovery, publishing, and subscriptions. Used by a curated roster of journalists and authors including Malcolm Gladwell, Erin Andrews, and Mitch Albom.

eras.builder_tagline: EM on the Bulletin Publishing UI team through its scale-up and sunset, placing every engineer who needed a new team and rebuilding mine around the back-end work that became Pro Mode. Stayed on as EM behind Pro Mode for Facebook Creators: the surface that bundled monetization, analytics, audience, and safety tools into one home for people building a creator business on Facebook.

achievements.text: Tech lead on Forecast, Meta's 0→1 social-first prediction market. Built on an internal points economy rather than real money, so accuracy and community discussion drove engagement instead of financial speculation.
Shipped in 2020: the same year Polymarket launched, the year before Kalshi got CFTC approval, and four years before either reached mainstream visibility around the 2024 election.
Set up the team's experimentation framework, driving the post-launch shift from rapid idea exploration to isolating the surfaces that drove growth and retention.
Personally shipped the buy/sell market page, scoring, leaderboards, and community feed from scratch, plus forecastapp.net, the public election-prediction surface for the 2020 US election.

items.caption: forecastapp.net (2020). Public election surface for Forecast, Meta's social prediction market. Aggregated forecasts on the 2020 US election were watched by journalists, election-night newsrooms, and the general public.
Forecast Trading (2020). The prediction market page inside Forecast: order flow, real-time pricing, and resolution rules. Used to forecast everything from elections to sports outcomes.
Forecast Feed (2021). Community feed of predictions, leaderboards, and market discussion threads. Used to keep in sync on the market & follow each other's positions and reasoning.
Forecast Motion (2021). External explainer animation showing how prices moved with volume across Forecast's prediction markets. Built to understand market mechanics and explain the platforms choices.

eras.builder_tagline: Led the engineering work behind a 0→1 social prediction market shipped out of NPE, Meta's new-product experimentation org: built the trading page, scoring, leaderboards, community feed, and forecastapp.net (the public election-prediction surface for the 2020 US election), all on an internal points economy where accuracy and community discussion beat speculation as the engagement driver. Shipped four years before Polymarket and Kalshi reached mainstream around the 2024 election.

achievements.text: Tech lead (team grew to 8) on the product Facebook's external fact-checking partners used to rate viral content on Facebook and Instagram. Launched with 5 partners; scaled to 80 organizations (including Reuters, AFP, and PolitiFact), hundreds of journalists, and 60 languages.

Architected the misinformation detection system from web links only (~σ% of posts) up to 100% of content across Facebook (posts, photos, video). Shipped Instagram support a quarter later, then Ads. The platform powered every misinformation policy launch after that and is still in production today.
Integrated with Meta’s content-deduplication so one journalist’s rating fanned out to Σ near-identical pieces per viral original across Facebook, Instagram, and Ads.

Shipped warning labels and friction surfaces on Facebook and Instagram with UXR, design, and policy, measurably cutting the share rate of fact-checked content. By the time I left, the work had grown into a dedicated Misinformation UI engineering team.

Architected misinformation detection from web links (~σ% of posts) to 100% of content across Facebook, Instagram, and Ads; one journalist’s rating fanned out to Σ near-identical pieces via content-deduplication.

items.caption: Fact-Checking UI (2018–20). The warning-label and friction surfaces shown to people who encountered content rated false on Facebook and Instagram (posts, photos, video, then Ads). Ratings authored by 80 partner organizations including Reuters, AFP, and PolitiFact, then fanned out via Meta's content-deduplication so one rating covered every near-identical copy.
Facebook Newsroom (2019). Public explainer on the third-party fact-checking program: the system, the partners, and the surfaces I led the engineering on.

eras.builder_tagline: Led the engineering work behind Facebook's response to viral misinformation: built the platform 80 journalism agencies across the globe used to rate content, the plumbing that fanned each rating out to every near-duplicate across Facebook, Instagram, and Ads, and the warning labels people saw when they tried to share it. Still in production today.

Shipped a data layer and UI that let users assemble topic anthologies and process them in real time across every post on Facebook and Instagram.

eras.builder_tagline: Main UI engineer on several of Meta's internal natural-language analytics tools, used across sales, communications, and safety: real-time election reporting alongside Fox News and other newsrooms, crisis monitoring around the world, and topic anthologies processed live across every post on Facebook and Instagram.
